_source_note: Draft checklist based on general burn-assessment guidance (TBSA / rule-of-nines / Lund-Browder, ANZCOR & WHO-aligned first aid principles). VERIFY against WHO/national burn-management guideline your team selects before final use. Not a diagnostic tool.

age.description: Age of the person (children/older adults burn more severely at same exposure)

cause_of_burn.description: Flame, hot liquid/scald, hot object contact, electrical, chemical

time_since_burn.description: How long ago the burn occurred and whether first aid (cooling) was already given

body_part_affected.description: Which part of the body - face, hands, feet, genitals, joints, or airway/around mouth-nose are always higher severity

approximate_size.description: Rough size of the burn area, e.g. smaller than a palm vs larger, or which body parts covered (proxy for %TBSA)

blistering_or_skin_appearance.description: Redness only vs blisters vs charred/white/leathery skin (depth indicator)

pain_level.description: Pain severity - note: full-thickness burns can be less painful due to nerve damage, which is itself a red flag

circumferential.description: Whether the burn goes all the way around a limb, finger, or the chest

smoke_or_enclosed_space_exposure.description: Whether burn happened in an enclosed space / near smoke (inhalation injury risk)
